How to read this page Each game opens on its chart: win rate per level, one series per config × persona, toggled from the matrix beside it, whose rows pick the config shown below. The Overview tab has one row per level, one column per persona, so skill tiers sit side by side. The number is the win rate (green ≥ 50%, orange below, red = never solved). Status: solved every seed won at least once · n/N seeds some did · unsolved none did. Click a card for its window — it opens on a one-line verdict, then the routes the agents took, the fastest win in gold. Hover, tap, or focus any ⓘ label for the definition; formulas and episode statuses are on the Instructions page.

Neuroevolution hyperparameters · mario · p10g40 · Rays

The brain — 291 weights, no gradients · rays sensing · inputs in [−1, 1] · outputs fire above 0.5 · left/right conflict → argmax
Sensing: 6 rays (250 px reach, 8 px steps) + enemy corridor + pit probe + q-block count + body state. Fitness: furthest x reached, +5,000 on a win (+ seconds left × persona time rate).
Genetic algorithm (GAConfig)
Sensors
rays
what the agent sees (exteroception)
Population
10
genomes evaluated per generation
Elite
4
best genomes copied unchanged
Tournament
k = 5
random genomes per pick, fittest wins
Crossover
70%
children bred from two parents (uniform mask)
Mutation rate
15%
share of weights nudged per child
Mutation σ
0.15
gaussian nudge size
Init σ
0.5
N(0, σ) starting weights
Anneal
×0.5
× mutation after a level's first win
Episode cap
60s
frames per attempt
Stall kill
5s
frames without progress → STUCK
Advance at
3 wins
wins in one gen → next curriculum level
Win bonus
+5,000
added to fitness on reaching the goal
Hidden
16
tanh units in the hidden layer

off
last move + jump fed back as 2 inputs

off
recurrent units looped back next frame

solved = every seed's population won at least once · partial (n/N seeds) = only some seeds cracked it · unsolved = no seed ever won. On the Overview it is the best across personas.Seeds whose population produced at least one WON episode within the budget.Share of episodes won in the 10 generations after the population's first win. Green means the population beats the level more often than not.How many generations evolution needed to solve the level once — the primary difficulty signal. Lower = easier.Wins divided by every episode of the whole probe, including early chaotic generations.Average in-game time of the winning runs only, ± the standard deviation of those win times (averaged across seeds).Generation at which the all-time best genome was found (mean ± 95% CI across seeds). Close to First win = the population peaks as soon as it solves the level.Rate of improvement: slope of best progress per generation, as a share of the level, measured from gen 1 to the generation the peak was first reached.Wall-clock time spent evolving on this level, summed over all seeds.How far through the level failing agents get on average (0% = start, 100% = goal).Average deaths per generation (one attempt per population member).Failed attempts (deaths and stalls) per win over the whole probe; with no wins, every one counts.Entropy of death locations: 0 = everyone dies at one learnable chokepoint, 1 = deaths scattered everywhere (feels random).The single failure mode that kills most agents: Enemy, Pit, Saw, Spike, Stall, OOB.Coins collected / coins available (100% when the level has none).Win rate in the last third of generations minus the first third — how much the population learned.Episodes ended by the stall detector (no forward progress for 5 seconds).Distinct route clusters among winning runs (needs 2+ wins with logged routes).Share of winning runs that follow the most common route. Near 100% = one true path.Challenge calibration: completion rate and win time vs the target band in code/stats/MarioThresholds.yaml. Bands are designer-set, not human-calibrated yet.Punishment severity: deaths per win and death spread vs their target bands.Strategy diversity: route-cluster count and dominant-path share vs their target bands.
